The biggest issue with the people who are disliking the season and finale comes down to a fundamental problem that has plagued online discussion for years now. People are more focused on creating “issues” in their head and plot holes that don’t exist to justify their distaste for what they watched. On top of that, people’s memories are so shot, they can’t even remember what happened 5 minutes previously. The amount of people who somehow missed that Ryan and Butcher lost their powers is depressing. No one is able to pay attention anymore. People have such a lack of understanding characters that it makes the say things that make no sense in the grand scheme of the show. Homelander wasn’t “ruined” at the end, it was exactly what we knew all along!

It's the 'business' part of show-business. Studio executives know that most people will watch the finale no matter what just to get closure, so why spend more money on it? And they aren't going after awards - those aren't earned nowadays but are paid for in advance by the studios anyway and they're certainly not here to leave some long lasting legacy. It's a trend with a lot of shows and movies nowadays and the superhero ones suffer the most because VFX takes a good chunk of a show/movie budget.

12:27 Coy is trying too hard to defend it. Great storytelling is great storytelling no matter the medium. Was it underwhelming? Definitely. It didn’t have to be an apocalypse level kind of thing, but simple writing, do the things you say your story and your characters are going to do, if you can’t and choose to go in another direction, all it would take is one or a few lines to address it. For me, this show has been doing a rinse and repeat since S2, just so they could get to their season 5. If your story cannot justify or answer questions on the actions taken by your characters, then obviously you have failed. If the decisions made by your characters are not within character, do not make sense for the story being told in the moment and only serve to set up a future narrative, then you have failed. There are much better shows out there that were told without the need of big battle scenes and it made sense for the story. And if you are saying, it was all in service of the characters, not necessarily the narrative, then I point you to shows that are much better character pieces than whatever that finale was trying to be: The Penguin, Peacemaker S1&2
